name: Frigate
description: Imports a Frigate NVR into the knowledge graph: Frigate as a service (URL, port, version) and its cameras as cameras (IP address or host name from the stream or ONVIF address, state, detect resolution, recording on/off, object detection, tracked objects), each "related to" the service. Contributes the kind camera (shared with the UniFi Protect plugin) with the relations "located in" a room and "powered by" a switch, outlet or smart plug. AI clients get the 50 most recent events (label, camera, score, start and end time, clip and snapshot available; optionally filtered by camera or label) and statistics (version, camera and detection rates, detector inference time, CPU and memory, storage). Read-only: only GET requests and the login. Stream credentials are never stored; only the host is read from stream addresses. Settings: url (e.g. https://frigate.example.org:8971, or http://<host>:5000 for the unauthenticated internal port), optional username and password (a Frigate user, 0.14 or later; the plugin logs in with POST /api/login on each run and uses the session token, a viewer role is enough), optional token (a fixed bearer token instead; Frigate session tokens expire, so username and password are preferred) and optional name (default: Frigate).

mcpTools.name: frigate.sync
mcpTools.description: Import Frigate and its cameras into the knowledge graph now.

mcpTools.name: frigate.events
mcpTools.description: The 50 most recent Frigate events: label (and sub label), camera, score in percent, start and end time (UTC), zones, whether a clip and a snapshot exist. Optional filters camera and label.

mcpTools.name: frigate.stats
mcpTools.description: Frigate statistics: version and latest version, uptime, frames and detections per second per camera, connection quality, detector inference time, CPU and memory use and storage usage in GiB.
